title: What they said at the time

clips.q: We are a different kind of toy store with a unique product mission and a passionate commitment to our customers. We believe that learning should be fun.
Shakeout in children’s multimedia retail continues
clips.who: **Publishers Weekly**, subheadline on the Noodle Kidoodle merger, May 1, 2000[^20]

clips.q: The key message here is that the stores are open and stock is on the shelves.
clips.who: **Rich Tauberman**, spokesman for Zany Brainy, Publishers Weekly, May 21, 2001[^21]

clips.q: Zany Brainy’s Chapter 11 filing was about liquidity. Zany Brainy has a strong brand and excellent store locations.
clips.who: **Kenneth J. Abdalla**, managing member of Waterton Management, Publishers Weekly, Jul 16, 2001[^22]

clips.q: The companies are the two most powerful kid’s brands in America today and are a perfect complement to each other.
clips.who: **Jerry R. Welch**, chairman and CEO of The Right Start, press release, Aug 16, 2001[^9]

clips.q: The current environment for toy retailers is awful.
clips.who: **Jerry R. Welch**, letter to FAO Inc. employees, quoted by Playthings, Dec 2, 2003[^18]

clips.q: That really hurt them. They’ve been struggling for quite some time.
clips.who: **An unnamed publisher**, on Zany Brainy’s systems and inventory-control problems, Publishers Weekly, Dec 8, 2003[^25]
